title: The Elders of the School of Rav
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Bava Kamma 75a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.75a.16) Rava said, “I defeated the elders of the school of Rav,” and [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Bava_Kamma.75a.16.1) explains that this is Rav Hamnuna, who is so called, as in [Sanhedrin 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.17b.6). Hyman objects that there they said only “in the school of Rav they say — Rav Hamnuna,” and [Tosafot](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Bava_Kamma.75a.16.1) there explain that it is Rav Huna.[^1]

notes.text: [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2768&lang=en) records the disagreement. Rashi takes Rav Hamnuna to be “the elders of the school of Rav.” Tosafot discusses that reading and favors another: Rava addresses Rav Hamnuna, who has prevailed over Rav Huna. The Sanhedrin passage discusses the formula “they say in the school of Rav,” the distinction Hyman draws here.
